title: Fleetdesk rental management
alt: Actual Fleetdesk vehicle-level availability showing a blocked vehicle, its real synthetic reservation dates and an available vehicle quotation action
desc: See which vehicles fit a rental period, quote and allocate safely, then search and export the saved reservation records.
built: Turned the rental overview into a vehicle-level decision workspace: explain blocking periods, preselect an available vehicle into the tested quotation flow, and search/export exactly the shown historical snapshots.
why: A rental workspace must prevent two customers from being promised the same vehicle for overlapping dates, and keep the reviewed price clear when records change.
how: Choose dates and inspect each vehicle’s advisory availability, including actual confirmed periods that block it.
Quote an available vehicle with its dates already selected; confirmation retains the tested allocation and price rechecks.
Combine reservation status filters with snapshot search, then export exactly the displayed records and saved integer-cent quotations.
demonstrates: Business workflow design, transactional allocation, accessible decision support, data integrity and independently verified record exports.
caption: Real availability disclosure from the working app: confirmed blocking periods and available-vehicle actions come from the same synthetic records and shared rules as the quotation workflow.
result: Existing record workflows and new rental workflows pass API/domain, browser-rule and full browser checks before this release. The isolated MySQL integration verifies simultaneous overlap rejection, retry identity, saved prices, referential integrity and state transitions. Desktop/mobile captures match this exact source revision; the linked run records its actual result.
limits: Synthetic educational application, with no real fleet, payments, tax/deposit calculation or deployed multi-user backend. The public demo is local to one browser profile and uses Web Locks to coordinate its tabs; it cannot allocate across devices. UTC dates use an exclusive return date. Early-return pricing, rental amendments and deletion of referenced history are outside scope. MySQL allocation safety assumes writes use the transactional service.
technical: Separate pure rental rules, memory/MySQL adapters and a presentation module preserve original CRUD routes. Python and JavaScript follow a 27-case rules contract. Memory uses a shared RLock; browser writes use an exclusive Web Lock and fresh storage read; MySQL confirmation locks the vehicle/customer rows in a transaction and preserves references with foreign keys. Request IDs prevent duplicate creation after a lost response. Integer-cent rate and name snapshots preserve quoted terms; stale rates require a new quote. The read-only availability roster delegates to those existing rules. Snapshot search and CSV formatting are isolated presentation helpers, independently checked with Python CSV parsing. Eleven browser journeys cover both Flask/static frontends, exact exports, keyboard focus and mobile decisions; all original MySQL contention checks remain.
run: Install requirements.txt; set DEMO_MODE=1 and run python CarServer.py. The README documents the non-destructive MySQL reservation migration and opt-in isolated integration checks. The public static demo shares its frontend and tested rules contract.

title: Breast cancer classification
alt: Genuine saved-results explorer showing logistic-regression confusion counts, malignant precision and recall, and a training-majority baseline
desc: Explore saved classifier errors, compare a training-majority baseline and see why accuracy alone can mislead.
built: Turned the reproducible three-model evaluation into an auditable, read-only results lab. Every confusion count and score comes from saved predictions, with a baseline selected only from training labels.
why: A high accuracy can hide systematically missed examples when classes are imbalanced. The project makes error types, denominators and evaluation limits visible before interpreting a model comparison.
how: Reproduce the existing fixed three-model evaluation with all 30 features and preprocessing inside training-only cross-validation.
Reconcile saved predictions with source rows, confusion matrices and scores; compute a majority baseline using training labels only.
Choose a saved classifier to explore its errors, malignant precision/recall/F1 and balanced accuracy; controls read results without retraining.
demonstrates: Reproducible machine learning, class-imbalance analysis, precise metric interpretation, data-integrity checks and accessible frontend development.
caption: Actual browser capture of the saved-results lab after desktop and mobile checks. The controls select previously computed outputs; they do not train a model.
result: Saved predictions from the unchanged three-model evaluation reconcile with source labels and confusion counts. Logistic regression: 7 missed / 64, Decision tree: 10 missed / 64, Random forest: 6 missed / 64. The training-majority baseline scores 62.6% accuracy but misses 64 of 64 malignant-labelled holdout examples. The explorer reports positive-class precision/recall/F1 and balanced accuracy without retraining. This repeatedly reused holdout is exploratory, with no independent or clinical validation.
limits: Educational analysis of a public teaching dataset, not a diagnostic system. This browser reads saved results only; it accepts no patient inputs and trains no models. The holdout has been reused across models and portfolio iterations, so it is exploratory rather than an untouched final test or an unbiased selection estimate. The baseline is context, not a new tuned classifier. No independent cohort, clinical validation, calibration study or causal feature interpretation is claimed.
technical: A Python export independently reconciles source hashes, fixed partitions, saved prediction labels, confusion counts and metrics before generating the explorer JSON. A training-majority baseline uses 250 benign and 148 malignant training labels. Malignant precision is explicitly undefined when a model predicts no positives; F1 is zero when it misses every positive. The existing evaluation, training-only five-fold CV and figure generation remain unchanged. Browser tests check all four approaches at desktop/mobile widths, keyboard selection, exact rendered values and loading failure.
run: Install requirements.txt, run python evaluate.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v, python plot_portfolio.py and python build_explorer.py. Serve docs/ with a local static server. npm ci and npm run test:browser run repeatable desktop/mobile checks. The original notebook remains separate.
gallery: releases/machine-learning/0ecd0b99d3d3bcb6cb4dc93835a48ba9d8bb6fa3/baseline.jpg
A baseline chosen from training labels reaches 62.6% holdout accuracy while missing all 64 malignant-labelled examples.
releases/machine-learning/0ecd0b99d3d3bcb6cb4dc93835a48ba9d8bb6fa3/comparison.png
Existing training-only CV and exploratory holdout results; fold SD is not a confidence interval.

challenge: Accuracy rewards majority guessing on an imbalanced dataset. The useful challenge is to explain which examples were missed and what each denominator means, without turning a reused exploratory holdout into a model-selection claim. The exporter cross-checks independent saved artifacts and carries their hashes into a browser that cannot train, tune or accept patient inputs.

title: Hotel booking prototype
alt: Actual hotel demonstration homepage with future date selection and credited illustrative bedroom photography
desc: A polished multi-step hotel demonstration with exact pricing, stable confirmation retries and recoverable booking reviews.
built: Preserved the established hotel interface and strengthened the shared booking rules and review lifecycle so date changes, expired sessions and repeated confirmations behave predictably.
why: A multi-step transaction should carry information reliably from one screen to the next. The project explores session state, validation and pricing across a booking journey.
how: Choose future dates, a room type and quantity; the shared rules calculate an exact integer-cent example total.
Enter sample guest details and review the quote. Changed or expired reviews are refreshed without losing the selection, and require explicit confirmation again.
Complete a demonstration confirmation, revisit it safely or edit dates and review a new quotation; no actual room is reserved.
demonstrates: Server-rendered web development, session handling, input validation and turning a multi-step process into a working application.
caption: Genuine capture of the verified shared interface. The hotel is fictional; photography is illustrative and credited. Browser-only public mode is labelled prominently.
result: Backend/rule regressions, an isolated MySQL 8.4 catalog check and complete browser journeys are required before release. Tests cover simultaneous confirmation identity, review expiry, strict numeric inputs, exact-cent totals, date changes, restored sessions, stale stored prices, reload/reset and mobile layout. The linked run identifies the exact tested revision.
limits: The hotel, rooms, prices and guest records are synthetic. Public Pages runs only the shared browser demonstration; it does not run Express or MySQL. Stock is illustrative per room type, not a date-based hotel inventory or a held allocation. Confirmations create no real reservation, payment, account or message. Review/receipt state is temporary; the bounded Express cache and local session store are educational rather than a production booking database.
technical: One shared JavaScript rules module serves Express and the static frontend. Rates use positive integer cents within the existing DECIMAL(10,2) catalog range; counts reject coercion and ambiguous numeric syntax. Reviews have a shared 15-minute lifetime. A bounded temporary token-keyed receipt cache keeps concurrent Express retries consistent; browser confirmation reuses the same reviewed receipt. Recovery refreshes session/catalog and review, preserving sample guest details while requiring a new explicit confirmation. CSRF and safe catalog errors remain enforced.
run: Run npm ci, npm test and npm start for Express at http://127.0.0.1:3000. No database is needed by default. npm run build:demo generates the public static version. An optional isolated MySQL Docker setup and opt-in integration test are documented separately.

title: Plant growth & statistics
alt: Genuine PlantGrowth explorer showing all thirty observations, group means and variability with selectable adjusted comparisons
desc: Explore every measurement, compare the size of group differences and keep statistical uncertainty visible.
built: Added an accessible comparison lab to the reproducible PlantGrowth investigation. Every observed value, mean, sample SD and adjusted comparison comes from the same computation as the preserved figures.
why: Differences in averages can be misleading without considering variability. This project shows how visual evidence and statistical testing support a careful comparison.
how: Inspect all thirty original measurements, three group summaries and pointwise mean intervals; exact source rows remain available in a table and CSV.
Select one of three saved Welch comparisons to inspect its raw mean difference, adjusted interval and adjusted p-value on a consistent axis.
Distinguish individual variability, uncertainty and practical importance without changing the method or inferring general treatment effectiveness.
demonstrates: Reproducible statistics, raw-unit effect interpretation, uncertainty communication, source-data integrity and accessible data visualisation.
caption: Actual comparison-lab browser capture. Circles are original measurements; horizontal offsets only separate points. Diamonds and bars show means and pointwise 95% intervals.
result: Thirty source observations, ten per group. Sample means: control 5.032, treatment 1 4.661, treatment 2 5.526 (dataset units). Primary Welch omnibus p=0.0174; classic ANOVA p=0.0159 is a sensitivity analysis. All three Welch comparisons use Bonferroni adjustment. Treatment 2 minus Treatment 1: +0.865 dataset units, adjusted 95% interval 0.085 to 1.645, adjusted p=0.0279. The explorer preserves all measurements and methods. No practical-benefit threshold or general treatment effectiveness is established.
limits: Thirty observations in a teaching dataset do not establish universal treatment effectiveness. Independence and the original experimental design cannot be verified from the CSV alone. Mean intervals assume approximate normality; Welch inference is a small-sample approximation. A p-value is neither an effect size nor the probability that the null hypothesis is true. Methods were selected for this educational investigation, not preregistered confirmatory analysis.
technical: The same in-memory observations, group summaries and Welch/Bonferroni results feed the original Matplotlib figures and the browser export. The build checks exact dataset bytes and attaches the source revision. Six Python regressions preserve reproducibility, independently reconcile classic F, verify every source row and sample SD, and compare adjusted pair intervals/degrees of freedom with the SciPy confidence-interval API. Three browser journeys check all pairs, exact rendered numbers, source table values, keyboard selection, desktop/mobile layout and loading failure. Methods are fixed; selecting a control only reads saved results.
run: Install requirements.txt, run python analyze_plants.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v and python build_explorer.py. Serve docs/ with a local static server. npm ci and npm run test:browser run repeatable desktop/mobile checks. Original CSV, saved calculations and coursework remain available.

A raw mean difference with its familywise adjusted interval, zero reference and practical-importance caveat.

challenge: A mean difference, individual variation and uncertainty describe different things. The lab keeps all observations visible and separates pointwise mean intervals from adjusted pairwise intervals. One computation supplies the figures, numerical summaries and interface, with an independent API reconciliation to catch drift. The interpretation explains why a statistically supported difference need not be practically useful.

title: Sorting algorithms, measured
alt: Actual Sort Lab table comparing key comparisons and index swaps for three traces on the same custom input
desc: Compare sorting work on the same input, inspect each real trace and keep operation counts separate from measured runtimes.
built: Extended Sort Lab with complete operation comparisons and validated custom inputs while preserving all five Python implementations, their tests and traceable benchmark observations.
why: Two methods can produce the same answer while taking very different amounts of work. Correctness and measurement help make that trade-off visible.
how: Choose a generated pattern/size or enter 1–24 whole numbers; the same unchanged starting input feeds all three browser traces.
Compare complete key-comparison/index-swap totals, then open any trace, step backwards/forwards or reset to that exact input.
Inspect the separately measured five-algorithm Python benchmark, whose unchanged implementation/output hashes preserve the original observations.
demonstrates: Algorithmic reasoning, controlled comparisons, state management, regression testing and accessible interactive explanation.
caption: Genuine browser capture: complete trace totals for one shared custom input. These are key comparisons and index exchanges in JavaScript, not elapsed time or Python benchmark measurements.
result: Five Python implementations passed correctness checks on 125 measured sorts: five identical seeded random samples at each size from 50 to 1,000. Median and IQR are calculated from saved raw measurements. Measurements were recorded on Windows-11-10.0.26300-SP0 with Python 3.12.2; unchanged algorithm hashes reuse those observations. The browser explorer compares complete key-comparison/index-swap totals for three actual traces on the same generated or validated custom input. Selecting a trace and resetting preserve its starting values. These operation counts and animation pace are separate from the recorded Python runtime measurements.
limits: Measurements cover random non-negative integer inputs from 50 to 1,000 in one recorded environment; they do not establish a universal ranking. IQR describes observed variation, not confidence. Rightmost-pivot recursive quicksort has adverse-input recursion limits. Radix supports non-negative integers and rejects booleans/fractions. The browser explorer ports only three approaches and limits inputs to 24 values; animation pace is unrelated to Python runtime.
technical: Seven Python tests preserve algorithm correctness and benchmark-cache provenance. Five Node checks compare final traces with actual Python outputs, preserve every intermediate multiset, reconcile independently known counts and validate custom input syntax/bounds. Three browser journeys verify all row-to-trace totals, duplicate/custom input, retained-input resets, invalid-input recovery, playback and dense 24-value mobile layout. Cached traces make algorithm selection reuse the exact same input. Swaps count exchanges between different indices, including equal values; self placements are shown but not counted. Bar heights share a scale across each input and zero values remain visible. Python algorithm bytes and recorded benchmark data are unchanged.
run: Install requirements.txt; run python benchmark_portfolio.py, python plot_portfolio.py and python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v. Use --refresh to request new measurements. For browser verification, build Python fixtures and docs, npm ci, npm run test:trace and npm run test:browser.

challenge: A comparison is only fair if every algorithm starts with the same values. The original controls regenerated input whenever the algorithm changed; deterministic examples hid that dependency. A shared current-input state and cached traces now keep custom values stable across selection, exploration and reset. Complete totals and in-progress counters are labelled separately, while the measured benchmark remains a separate experiment.

title: Iris dataset exploration
alt: Working Iris observation explorer with native species and feature controls, actual source points and checked summary cards
desc: Filter species, compare any pair of Iris measurements and inspect the original rows behind independently checked summaries.
built: Built an interactive observation lab over the preserved 150-row analysis, with species filters, four-feature selectors, exact source tables and filtered CSV downloads.
why: Before choosing a model, it helps to see how measurements vary and which features reveal useful structure. Clear exploratory analysis makes a dataset easier to understand.
how: Choose observed species and any horizontal/vertical feature; axis ranges stay fixed as species change.
Compare browser-computed means and sample SD with independent Python reference summaries.
Inspect every selected source row or download all four original measurements and supplied species labels.
demonstrates: Data provenance, descriptive statistics, independent numerical checks, accessible interactive graphics and reproducible publication.
caption: Actual working explorer: original observations use species-specific shapes and colours; summary cards show sample means and SD in centimetres.
result: 150 supplied observations, 50 per species. Mean petal lengths: Setosa 1.462 cm, Versicolor 4.260 cm, Virginica 5.552 cm. Setosa forms a distinct petal cluster in these observations; Versicolor and Virginica overlap. All four measurements and all species labels are observed data, not model predictions. Repeated measurement rows are retained; this descriptive teaching sample does not establish general classification performance.
limits: This is descriptive exploration of a small, familiar teaching dataset. Separation in these observations is not independent validation of a classifier or evidence of general performance. Pooled correlations mix species and do not establish causation. Identical measurement rows are retained because equality alone does not prove duplicate sampling. The supplied CSV is preserved; historical Iris variants differ in two documented observations.
technical: The original analysis now also exports every source row and twelve reference summaries. Five Python regressions reconcile original rows, historical variants, provenance and statistics; two Node checks cover sample SD and CSV semantics; three browser journeys cover all sixteen feature pairings, filters, exports, failed loading and narrow layouts. Generated build metadata stays untracked. Original coursework and data remain intact.
run: Install requirements.txt; run python explore_iris.py, python -m unittest discover -p "test_*.py" -v and python build_explorer.py. Run npm ci, npm run test:rules, npx playwright install chromium and npm run test:browser. Serve docs locally to explore.

Every feature pair is checked, repeated rows retain their original order, and the source hash and documented variant travel with the release.
